about: Catalogue of IB AA SL exam question types, built from the per-part tags of the Math-AA question bank (RktRobinhood/Math-AA---Question-Bank). Structures are described in our own words; no IB text, numbers or images. See curriculum/QUESTION_TYPES.md. Check and regenerate with node tools/question-types.mjs.
partIds: A part ID is the bank question ID plus "." and the part letter (aa-sl-2021-may-tz1-p1-q01.a). Questions with no lettered parts use the bare question ID.

levels.0: Prior learning: algebra the IB assumes (factorising, rearranging, surds, fractions). Floor 1 warm-ups, and served when a dependent step is missed.
levels.1: Recall, 1 to 2 marks, one step. Floor 1.
levels.2: Procedure, 3 to 4 marks, one skill in a few steps. Floors 1 to 2.
levels.3: Paper 1 exam level, 5 to 6 marks, no calculator. Floors 2 to 3.
levels.4: Paper 2 exam level, 5 to 6 marks with a calculator, or a harder multi-condition Paper 1 item. Floor 3 and deeper.
levels.5: Synoptic: Section B chains, concept links and modelling. Bosses, floor 4 and deeper.

quadratic.name: One parabola in all its forms
quadratic.summary: Pick a and the two roots (or the vertex), then derive every linked quantity, so any of them can be hidden and any shown.

quantities.name: a
quantities.is: leading coefficient: the stretch, and up (a > 0) or down (a < 0)
quantities.pick: non-zero; ±1, ±2, ±1/2 on Paper 1, ±3 allowed when nothing is halved

quantities.name: p, q
quantities.is: the roots, so the x-intercepts are (p, 0) and (q, 0)
quantities.pick: integers with p < q; p + q even whenever the axis or vertex is asked

quantities.name: h
quantities.is: axis of symmetry x = h, and the x-coordinate of the vertex

quantities.name: k
quantities.is: y-coordinate of the vertex: the minimum (a > 0) or maximum (a < 0) value
quantities.pick: f(h) = −a(q − p)²/4

quantities.name: b, c
quantities.is: coefficients of the general form ax² + bx + c
quantities.pick: b = −a(p + q), c = apq

quantities.name: y-intercept
quantities.pick: c = apq = ah² + k

quantities.name: Δ
quantities.pick: a²(q − p)²

quantities.name: forms
quantities.is: general ax² + bx + c, factorised a(x − p)(x − q), vertex a(x − h)² + k
quantities.pick: all three written from a, p, q

quantities.name: range
quantities.is: y ≥ k when a > 0, y ≤ k when a < 0
quantities.pick: from a and k

quantities.name: extra point
quantities.is: (x₁, f(x₁)) used to pin down a
quantities.pick: small integer x₁, not a root and not h

quantities.name: table
quantities.pick: centred near h so a symmetric pair of equal outputs is visible

modes: rational roots (default): all three forms exist with integer p and q
surd roots: pick integers h, k with −k/a positive and not a square, so the roots are h ± √(−k/a) and there is no rational factorised form
no real roots: pick h, k with k/a > 0, so Δ < 0 and there is no factorised form over the reals
clean: Paper 1: every value exact; with q − p even, k is an integer or a half
the extra point has small integer coordinates
on a graph, roots, vertex and y-intercept sit on grid points
roots, vertex and y-intercept are distinct points unless a view needs them to coincide

quadratic-equation.name: A quadratic equation, in context or in disguise
quadratic-equation.summary: The quadratic situation set equal to zero, wrapped in a context or a substitution that makes exactly one root unusable.

quantities.name: wrapper
quantities.pick: plain; context (lengths, a sector, probabilities that sum to 1); u = bˣ; x + c/x; a sum of logs

quantities.name: u-roots
quantities.is: the roots of the quadratic in u
quantities.pick: integers, one of them ≤ 0 when u = bˣ so it must be rejected

quantities.name: x-roots
quantities.is: the solutions of the original equation
quantities.pick: from the u-roots: x = log_b u; for logs, keep only roots with every argument positive

quantities.name: invalid root
quantities.is: the root the wrapper rules out
quantities.pick: exactly one: a negative length, a probability outside [0, 1], bˣ ≤ 0 or a log of a non-positive number

clean: Paper 1: u-roots are integers and the valid x is an integer or log_b of an integer
Paper 2 context versions may need the formula and 3 s.f.

quadratic-parameter.name: A quadratic with a parameter in it
quadratic-parameter.summary: A quadratic whose coefficients contain an unknown constant k (directly, or after equating a line and a curve), so its discriminant is an expression in k.

quantities.name: source
quantities.pick: given directly (x² + kx + 9); a line y = mx + n meeting a curve y = x² + px + r; a log or exponential equation that reduces to a quadratic

quantities.name: k
quantities.pick: in b, in c, or in both

quantities.name: Δ(k)
quantities.is: the discriminant as an expression in k
quantities.pick: linear or quadratic in k; for a line meeting y = x² + px + r it is (p − m)² − 4(r − n)

quantities.name: critical k
quantities.pick: integers: for the line case pick r − n = s², so m = p ± 2s

quantities.name: condition
quantities.pick: equal roots or tangent (Δ = 0), two points (Δ > 0), none (Δ < 0), real roots (Δ ≥ 0), always positive (a > 0 and Δ < 0)

quantities.name: extra condition
quantities.is: a second requirement on the roots or k
quantities.pick: same-sign roots (c/a > 0), k positive, or the log argument staying positive

quantities.name: contact point
quantities.pick: x = −b/(2a) at the critical k

clean: critical k values are integers
the inequality in k factorises
say whether the boundary is included

curve-and-line.name: A curve and a line that meet
curve-and-line.summary: Pick the two meeting x-values first, then build the curve as the line plus a multiple of (x − x₁)(x − x₂), so the equated quadratic is known in advance.

quantities.name: line
quantities.is: y = mx + n, or the normal to the curve at a given point
quantities.pick: small integer m and n; m ≠ 0

quantities.name: x₁, x₂
quantities.pick: integers, or h ± √d with small d

quantities.name: curve
quantities.is: a quadratic y = mx + n + a(x − x₁)(x − x₂), or a rational y = c + e/(x − r) chosen to meet the line at x₁ and x₂
quantities.pick: a non-zero integer; for the rational curve r is not x₁ or x₂

quantities.name: equated quadratic
quantities.pick: a(x − x₁)(x − x₂) = 0, expanded

quantities.name: points
quantities.is: (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) on the line
quantities.pick: y = mx + n at each

quantities.name: distance
quantities.is: length of the chord between the points
quantities.pick: |x₂ − x₁|·√(1 + m²)

clean: Paper 1: integer or simple surd x-values; choose m = 0, ±1, ±2 or ±3 so √(1 + m²) is small
the final surd simplifies to a√b

quadratic-inequality.name: A quadratic compared with a number
quadratic-inequality.summary: The quadratic situation with an inequality sign and, sometimes, a right-hand side to move across first.

quantities.name: right-hand side
quantities.is: the value f(x) is compared with
quantities.pick: 0, or a constant d with f(x) − d still factorising

quantities.name: solution set
quantities.is: one interval between the roots, two rays outside them, all x, or no x
quantities.pick: from the sign of a, the roots and the sign

quantities.name: context bound
quantities.is: the largest or smallest whole number allowed
quantities.pick: Paper 2: non-integer roots, so the rounding direction matters

clean: Paper 1 roots are integers or simple fractions
Paper 2 roots are not integers, so the integer answer is a real decision

quadratic-model.name: A quadratic model in context
quadratic-model.summary: A projectile height h(t) or an area A(x) under a fixed-length constraint, built from the vertex so the optimum is clean.

quantities.name: context
quantities.pick: height of a thrown object over time; area of a pen with a fixed length of fence (with or without a wall)

quantities.name: peak
quantities.is: time and height of the maximum, or the width and area of the best pen
quantities.pick: vertex (T, H) with integer or half-integer T

quantities.name: a
quantities.pick: height: −5 or −4.9 (Paper 2); area: −1 or −2 from the constraint

quantities.name: start value
quantities.pick: h(0) = aT² + H

quantities.name: landing time
quantities.pick: T + √(−H/a); the negative root is rejected

quantities.name: constraint
quantities.pick: pen against a wall: A(x) = x(L − 2x), best x = L/4; free pen: A(x) = x(L/2 − x), best x = L/4 (a square)

clean: Paper 1: integer vertex and an integer or surd landing time
Paper 2: a = −4.9 and answers to 3 s.f.

fn-pre-expand.name: Brackets to expand
fn-pre-expand.summary: Small integer coefficients in one or two brackets, sometimes with a factor in front and a constant after.

quantities.name: brackets
quantities.pick: k(x + r)(x + s) + d, or k(x + r)² + d, with small integers

quantities.name: expanded
quantities.pick: computed from the brackets

clean: coefficients between −9 and 9
answers have at most three terms

fn-pre-factorise.name: An expression with known factors
fn-pre-factorise.summary: Pick the factors first, then expand, so the answer is known.

quantities.name: factors
quantities.pick: common factor kx; (x − r)(x − s); (mx + r)(x + s); (px − q)(px + q)

quantities.name: expression
quantities.pick: computed from the factors

clean: r and s between −9 and 9
leading coefficient at most 6

fn-pre-surds.name: Surds built from a square factor
fn-pre-surds.summary: Pick a and a square-free b, then show √(a²b) or sums of such surds.

quantities.name: a, b
quantities.pick: a from 2 to 6, b square-free from 2, 3, 5, 6, 7

quantities.name: shown
quantities.pick: √(a²b), sums, products, or (m ± √(a²b))/n with n dividing m and a

clean: every answer simplifies to integers and one surd

fn-pre-linear-inequalities.name: A linear inequality with a known boundary
fn-pre-linear-inequalities.summary: Pick the boundary and direction, then build ax + b compared with c.

quantities.name: boundary
quantities.pick: an integer or a simple fraction

quantities.name: sign of a
quantities.pick: negative in about half the items

quantities.name: form
quantities.pick: ax + b < c, or c₁ < ax + b ≤ c₂

clean: integer boundaries on Paper 1 style items

concepts.prompt: In y = a(x − h)² + k, k is increased while a and h stay the same. What happens to the vertex, the axis and the roots?
concepts.answer: The vertex moves straight up, the axis does not move, and the roots move towards the axis (for a > 0) until they merge and then vanish.

concepts.prompt: The axis of symmetry of y = ax² + bx + c passes through the y-intercept.
concepts.answer: Sometimes: only when b = 0, because the axis is x = −b/(2a) and the y-intercept is on x = 0.

concepts.prompt: Two quadratics with the same roots have the same vertex.
concepts.answer: False. They share the axis (the midpoint of the roots), but the vertex height k = −a(q − p)²/4 depends on a.

misconceptions.text: Uses x = b/(2a), dropping the minus sign
misconceptions.wrong: x = b/(2a), the mirror image of the true axis

misconceptions.text: Writes the axis as y = h, or just the number h, instead of x = h
misconceptions.wrong: y = h, or the bare number h

misconceptions.text: Reads h from a(x + 3)² as +3
misconceptions.wrong: x = −h, read from (x + h) with the sign kept

misconceptions.text: From a(x + 3)² − 4 gives the vertex (3, −4) instead of (−3, −4)
Finds the x-coordinate of the vertex but not the y-coordinate
misconceptions.wrong: working stops at x = h and gives the vertex as that number

misconceptions.text: Calls the vertex a minimum when a < 0
misconceptions.wrong: "minimum" when a < 0, or "maximum" when a > 0

misconceptions.text: Forgets to subtract the square of half the coefficient, writing x² − 8x + 11 = (x − 4)² + 11
misconceptions.wrong: (x − h)² + c, so k = c

misconceptions.text: When a ≠ 1, does not multiply the correction term by a
misconceptions.wrong: a(x − h)² + c − h², the correction not multiplied by a

misconceptions.text: Gets the sign of h wrong, writing (x + 4)² for x² − 8x + …
misconceptions.wrong: a(x + h)² + k

misconceptions.text: From (x + 1)(x − 4) gives the intercepts 1 and −4
misconceptions.wrong: x-intercepts at −p and −q

misconceptions.text: Leaves out the leading coefficient a when writing a(x − p)(x − q)
misconceptions.wrong: (x − p)(x − q) with a dropped

misconceptions.text: Thinks the y-intercept is pq rather than apq
misconceptions.wrong: pq instead of apq

concepts.prompt: A parabola has vertex (2, −8) and passes through (0, 4). Predict the sign of a before finding it, then check.
concepts.answer: Positive: the point is above the vertex, so the curve opens upwards. Check: 4 = a(0 − 2)² − 8 gives a = 3.

concepts.prompt: Any three points lie on exactly one quadratic y = ax² + bx + c.
concepts.answer: False. Three collinear points force a = 0 (a line), and two points with the same x but different y fit no function at all.

concepts.prompt: Two parabolas both have roots 1 and 5. One passes through (0, 5), the other through (0, −10). What does a say about each?
concepts.answer: y-intercept = 5a, so a = 1 for the first (opens up) and a = −2 for the second (opens down and is twice as steep).
